(Today through Wednesday)...
Issued at 305 AM EDT Thu Oct 29 2026

Surface analysis early this morning shows strong high pressure in 
place over the east coast, extending its influence far southwest, 
into the deep south and through the Ohio Valley. A cold front was 
stretching from WI across eastern IA to KS. Strong high pressure was 
found in the wake of the front over the Dakotas and MT. GOES19 shows 
a thin area of clouds along and ahead of the front over WI and IL. 
Some limited precipitation was found along the front.

Aloft, mainly a zonal flow was in place and water vapor showed 
subsidence in place ahead and in the wake of the front. Water vapor 
showed a thin band of moisture associated with the frontal boundary. 
Dew points were in the upper 40s and lower 50s.

Today...

The zonal flow aloft will remain in place today, quickly pushing the 
main upper trough over western Ontario east. As this occurs, the 
associated cold front will become elongated and best forcing 
dynamics looks to pass well to the north of Indiana. HRRR suggests 
some isolated late afternoon showers will be possible mainly in the 
OKK-LAF areas as the front passes, but confidence for this remains 
rather low. Only small chances may be included and most locations 
will remain dry. The noticeable things in the weather today will be 
an occasional wind gust this afternoon ahead of the front and the 
warm air mass ahead of the front. The southwest winds will allow for 
good mixing and high temperatures will reach the upper 70s. A few 
80s are not our of the question. Expect mainly a mostly sunny day as 
forecast soundings remain dry. However, clouds will arrive late this 
afternoon and evening as the front arrives and passes.

Friday and Saturday...

The zonal upper flow wanes on Friday as ridging begins to develop 
over the Mississippi Valley and builds across Indiana through 
Saturday. Within the lower levels, strong high pressure in the wake 
of Today/s front will push across the Great lakes and reach middle 
Atlantic states on Saturday. This large high will continue to 
dominate the weather across the eastern half of the country, 
providing mainly dry weather. Forecast soundings are on board with 
this, showing a dry column on both Friday and Saturday. Highs on 
these days will be a bit cooler than Today due to the arrival of the 
new, cooler, Canadian high pressure system, but still remain well 
above normals.

Sunday through Wednesday...

A more active weather pattern is expected to take shape late this 
weekend and into early next week. The upper level pattern is 
suggested to the become more progressive and southwesterly as a warm 
and moist subtropical jet stream across the southwestern United 
States and into the middle Mississippi and Ohio Valleys takes shape. 
A first wave looks to pass on Saturday night into Sunday. Forecast 
soundings at that point shows a deeply saturated column with pwats 
over 1.25 inches.

Models are differing a bit on the timing of an deep upper trough 
pushing through the NW parts of the country on Monday through 
Wednesday. Nonetheless, the southwest flow aloft looks to push 
embedded short waves and forcing dynamics into Indiana on Monday 
through Wednesday. Again, forecast soundings each of these days 
suggest deep saturation and high pwats.

Within the lower levels during this time, large high pressure looks 
to be set up east of the mid Atlantic states on Sunday, still 
dominating the weather across the eastern half of the country. 
However, warmer and humid southerly flow will be in across Indiana, 
essentially starting an overrunning situation as the upper forcing 
begins to arrive. By Tuesday and Wednesday, strong low pressure 
associated with the approaching upper trough is shown to develop 
over the Plains states, continuing to provide lift and forcing. 
Again, models differ a bit with the progression and orientation of 
the system, but still plenty of ingredients as listed above remain 
present to include chances for rain.

No significant intrusions of cold air is expected, thus above normal 
temperatures with highs in the 60s will continue to be expected.
